page: The Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is an entry-level virtual server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a single dedicated physical x86_64 core running an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, backed by 32 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant divergence between single-threaded execution and parallel throughput. In single-core testing, the instance scored 1956.0 in Geekbench and placed in the top tier on stress-ng single-core operations with 3373.08 points. It also achieved strong results in data processing, posting 31.57 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.38 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory bandwidth is balanced, registering 40.43 GB/sec read and 36.8 GB/sec write. However, overall multi-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core (1930.0), PassMark CPU (2969.39), and static web serving throughput (1.69 GB/sec), rank in the lowest percentiles due to the single-core limitation.

With its 8 GB memory capacity and dedicated execution thread, the voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd offers balanced resource efficiency for light memory-oriented services without the interference of shared-core scheduling. It is suited for lightweight caching services, small background workers, configuration managers, internal automation tasks, and modest single-threaded database or application workloads requiring NVMe storage.
description: The Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is a dedicated single-core instance belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute tier. Driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz with 32 MB L3 cache, it delivers 8.0 GB of memory and a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1956.0 and top-tier stress-ng single-core results, while achieving 31.57 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, aggregate multi-core and throughput-heavy operations are strictly constrained by the single-core hardware profile, as reflected in low PassMark and web serving scores. This hardware configuration is suitable for lightweight background workers, small memory-focused databases, local caching, and low-concurrency internal utilities requiring dedicated compute resources.
